content.introduction: The information technology sector includes industries such as IT Services, Semiconductor & Semiconductor Equipment, Software, and Technology Hardware Storage & Peripherals, all defined by the Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS®). The performance of these sectors is represented by the S&P 500 GICS® indices, with the latest changes showing the S&P 500 Semiconductor & Semiconductor Equipment Industry at +1772.44% and the S&P 500 Software Industry at +618.72% over the last period. The S&P 500 Information Technology Sector is part of the broader S&P 500, which had a nominal change of +12.81% as of the latest reported date.

U.S. Sectors & Industries Performance is represented by the S&P 500 GICS® (Global Industry Classification Standard) indices. Market Cap is the sum of the market value of each company assigned to the applicable GICS sector or industry. Several of the 69 industries do not have companies represented in the S&P 500 Index; therefore, performance is not available for those industries. Standard & Poor's 500 (S&P 500) Index is an unmanaged market-weighted index of 500 of the nation's largest stocks from a broad variety of industries. S&P 500 market weight is based on S&P Dow Jones Indices and represents the sum of the market cap of the companies in the applicable S&P 500 GICS sector index as a percentage of the total S&P 500 Index market capitalization. Sector weighting recommendations are provided by independent, third-party research firms to help further refine your analysis. Every business cycle is different, and so are the relative performance patterns among equity sectors.
